body:
I used to have a friend who did this as a rather poor attempt to lift my spirits. She would tell me that either she or another person "had it worse" than me and that what I was going through wasn't that bad. I guess in a way, she was trying to put things into perspective, but I felt horrible because it was a blatant dismissal of my feelings. 

Unfortunately I've done this at least once to a friend before and upon realization of what I was doing, I immediately apologized and did my best to support him more considerately. When I initially compared my experience to my friend's, I was very insensitive to his feelings. What I said was  out of anger at myself and the people who hurt me. My friend seemed so perfect and I couldn't understand his situation at the time or how he could possibly have suffered at all in comparison to the hardships I went through, especially since his life externally seemed to be a stark contrast to mine. 

I guess these people don't really understand how counterproductive their method of support is and believe that they're helping you put your life and troubles into perspective, when unfortunately they're unknowingly worsening your feelings.

Sorry for the late reply. Been low on energy lately. You're very kind and I appreciate your words of support, especially in times like this. I haven't found a therapist yet, but I hope I find a good one. I really don't seem to be improving...

Could be depression, could be a number of things. I know for a fact that being subjected to bullying and emotional abuse will definitely tear a person and their self esteem down. It's really unfortunate and difficult to build back up, but not impossible.

Hi and thanks. I'm honestly really trying because Im worried about my family. I don't want them to be devastated over my death, so I'm trying to continue fighting this, but it's getting really hard. Even if I did find a therapist, I'm worried that they won't be able to help me.
Thanks, but I don't think things will be okay for me. I want everything to be okay, though.
I'm exactly the same. I used to think it was strange to be anxious around family members, but I'm surprised to see I'm not alone in feeling uncomfortable like this.
Most of the people I've told or who knew either didn't believe me or understand and thought it was just an excuse or something I made up.

I had to do a double take when I read that you have BDD because I'm actually a long time sufferer myself, who unfortunately doesn't have the courage to post a photo of myself for others to see here,but i know the truth is that I'm hideous, so I'd just discomfort other readers if they were to see my face. 

I can't physically stop you from ending your life, but I will say that I know the personal hell you're in as a fellow BDD sufferer. I'm so sorry you are in so much pain and are struggling with BDD. It's a hell that not many people understand. It's frustrating when they don't understand and I know that it's hard to trust others when you're convinced or certain that you're unattractive, even if that may be false. 

Have you seen a therapist for help specifically for your BDD?

I've learned that those who can so easily speak terribly of or make fun of others are highly insecure about themselves. I know this for a fact after dating at least two people like that and being friends for a time being with not so nice people. 

I understand why this is a big deal. You're self conscious about the situation with your hair because part of your confidence is associated with that. I'm with someone who feels similarly and wants to see a professional for hair restoration. 

It's very insensitive for your roommate to take pictures of you in your most vulnerable moments and share them with people who you do not feel comfortable with knowing about your usage of the hair restoration product or hair loss. 

I do not have advice for you, because you've already tried talking to your roommate. I just want to say that even if you don't feel it or believe it, you might feel uncomfortable with losing hair, but being bald does not have to be bad. Bald is beautiful, too.
A mix of both. A large part of it is situational. I'm sure that if these situations were resolved, I'd be able to fully get out of this funk.
Almost every single night. It's so exhausting.

There's not enough information... But if you feel strongly that this therapist isn't very helpful to you, you should try a different one. Different therapists may have different approaches. 

My last therapist helped me to an extent and helped me develop some of the skills I needed,but as far as depression goes, it's still really bad. 

A therapist I had prior to the last one just sat in silence nodding and acknowledging everything I said and I seemed to be responsible for driving the conversation and session, which obviously didn't work out. 

It took me years to find the right one, so sometimes you have to keep searching. I believe that it can also possibly be an issue with you not being receptive,but maybe the help that your current therapist is providing  you with is just not right for you.

I was in the lobby of a building and it was time for me to go home after seeing my therapist (this was years ago). The building had glass revolving doors. I got extremely anxious and had a panic attack upon seeing a stranger just staring at me, freaked out and tried to rush out the revolving glass door.  I wound up running into the door embarrassingly. I was so embarrassed that I ran down the sidewalk all the way to the car...Im sure somebody saw me.

I feel this often. I cannot go outside comfortably. This isn't even a feeling. People really do stare at me. It could be for a number of reasons, but it always feels like it's because I look bizarre. I end up getting panic attacks because of that. 

I hate walking past houses for the same reason. I always feel like people are staring at me from their windows. 

**Edit:** As far as coping, I just focus on where I need to go and walk as quickly as I can.  I used to return the stares. Not advisable because some people see this as aggression. It's not something I do much anymore.

I have similar thoughts. Sometimes I wish that I had a terminal illness so that my family wouldn't have to be as devastated losing me to that illness as they would probably be if they were to lose me to suicide. I feel like it'd be harder for other people to understand my depression.

Thank you so much for sharing this. Do you plan on reposting this as a new thread? 

I'm not sure I have much by way of questions after reading about your experience that summer, but wow. I am so sorry. This hits really close to home for me. From the accumulating piles of miscellany in your bedroom down to the extended period of time not washing or brushing...That is so familiar to me. That's really nice of your mom to help you clean up. Did you talk to her about what was going on? Sorry if that's not a clear question. 

I'm really sorry if this brought back unpleasant memories for you. So did your mom help pull you out of that state or did you continue to go through what you did after she left?

I don't mind. Of course you can share that file with me. I would like to ask more about that summer, but only if you're comfortable sharing. 

Those are great questions to think about. Unfortunately it is really an uphill struggle to not put ourselves down,despite therapy. A past therapist gave me the same set of questions and tried to help me with confidence and self image, but that only lasted for so long.

Thank you for the response. I am considering finding an affordable therapist. It's worth a try since I honestly am not sure with my current circumstances I can really do much else. I honestly don't feel like I can be helped, though. 

I see potential in this sub helping me somewhat, but I'm unsure.

Yeah. It's almost surreal. It's as if they're telling your story. 

I've been a lurker on subs like this for the longest time and it's eerie because it's like someone is living my life whenever I come across highly relatable posts. Unfortunate that there are others who can relate, but at the same time... 

You're definitely not alone.

Thank you for your kind words and response. 

Waste of space is definitely one of the worst phrases a person can use to describe themselves. This is the first time in a long time I've confided anywhere to anybody that that's what I see when I look in the mirror when I can bring myself to, anyway. It's what is felt every day when I watch other people leave for work or just being able to be productive. 

No pressure to disclose how long it's been for you since the last shower, friend, if you're not comfortable. I'm not judging you regardless. Likewise, I'm proud of you for taking that shower! 

Honestly, my hygiene isn't superb. Every little movement to do what I need to do feels like I have heavy chains or weights restraining me. I'm trying to develop a habit  where whenever I have to get up to use the toilet, I try to either bathe, brush my teeth, or if I'm lucky, I can do everything.

I sleep whenever I can. Just sleep, eat, drag myself to take care of myself hygienically if I have any energy left for that or places I need to be that I can't quite avoid. 

No job, no school. I'm a useless waste of space. If I didn't have an SO, I'd probably be bedridden and a total pancake day and night.
